key_insight: An EHR-integrated generative AI tool identified inpatient VTE risk more sensitively than a checklist-based order set and slightly better than clinician judgment, though with lower specificity.
clinical_relevance: This suggests AI could help improve risk-appropriate thromboprophylaxis decisions in hospital workflows, especially when narrative chart details are important.
method: Multisite retrospective validation at Johns Hopkins Medicine
500 randomly sampled inpatient admissions balanced by site and order-set period
Compared iHGR and clinician-selected order sets against physician-adjudicated chart review as the reference standard
evidence_signal: In this real-world evaluation, iHGR achieved 81.8% sensitivity and 70.9% specificity, with performance compared directly against two workflow-based order set approaches.
watch_item: False negatives were linked to missed narrative risk factors, highlighting that documentation quality and human oversight remain important for safe implementation.
paper_title: Multisite Real-World Validation of an Electronic Health Record-Integrated Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool for Venous Thromboembolism Risk Stratification
